concepts.description: The foundational laws relating forces to the motion of bodies, covering inertia, F=ma, and action-reaction pairs. They form the starting point of the classical mechanics review.
concepts.name: Newton's Three Laws Of Motion

concepts.description: In conservative force fields the total mechanical energy of a system remains constant over time. This principle is studied as a key consequence of conservative forces.
concepts.name: Conservation Of Energy

concepts.description: A reformulation of classical mechanics derived from the principle of least action, using generalized coordinates and the Lagrangian function. It provides an alternative framework to Newtonian analysis.
concepts.name: Lagrangian Mechanics

concepts.description: The total linear momentum of an isolated system stays constant when no external net force acts on it. It is reviewed as one of the fundamental conservation laws of mechanics.
concepts.name: Conservation Of Linear Momentum

concepts.description: A reformulation of mechanics using generalized coordinates and momenta together with the Hamiltonian function, which typically represents total energy. It extends the Lagrangian approach into phase space.
concepts.name: Hamiltonian Mechanics

concepts.description: The total angular momentum of a system is conserved when the net external torque is zero. It is covered alongside linear momentum as a central conservation principle.
concepts.name: Conservation Of Angular Momentum

concepts.description: The variational principle stating that the path a system takes makes the action functional stationary. It is the basis from which Lagrangian mechanics is derived.
concepts.name: Principle Of Least Action

concepts.description: Oscillatory motion in which the restoring force is proportional to displacement from equilibrium. It serves as a canonical example for applying the mechanics frameworks reviewed.
concepts.name: Simple Harmonic Motion
